name: Durban
blurb: Recent discussions highlight Durban as a host for cultural and film festivals, international summits like SADC, and sporting events involving the Sharks rugby team. Visitors frequently note the city's distinct local cuisine, including traditional Durban curries, and regional attractions such as beaches and gardens.

positive: Praise for unique local Durban curries
Appreciation for cultural events and film festivals
Interest in local gardens and landmarks like the lotus-shaped temple
negative: Complaints about expensive flight ticket options between Johannesburg and Durban
Reports of dangerous driving and speeding on the N3 road to Durban

quotes.text:
Judges who attended a conference in Durban expressed alarm when they were quoted plane ticket options at R9,000 for return flights between Johannesburg and Durban. These tickets normally cost about R3,000.

Read groundup.org.za/article/unan... by Nathan Geffen

I'm just back from a Karoo desert road trip and the desert roads were chill and beautiful (and rains have brought the flowers out), but on the main roads - N1 Cape to Joburg, N3 to Durban - the speeding and overtaking with no care for others was horrific.

This is not a post about speeding either.
Don't forget about the second largest Indian population outside of India in Durban South Africa where curries are unique in their own way.

ZA Day 3 - Durban Chicken Curry with Rice and Malva Cake.

Google says curry is unique as it uses only onions & tomato to thicken the sauce, the fat must separate and has to be spicy hot.  Very similar to many south East Asian curries.

Malva cake could come from the Afrikaner word for marshmallow.
